top_choice_rationale: P001 (B022: Autor, Hanson, Dorn) ranks first on the common criteria of originality, testing and attributable credit. The China-shock and local-labour-market work turned a broad question into a measurable one with transparent designs. A decade of replication and re-analysis has contested the size and persistence of the effects, not the finding that adjustment is slow and costly. Autor, Dorn and Hanson are joint authors of the central papers. A citation confined to empirical analyses of technology and import competition, without 'conceptual' wording, avoids claiming the task-model theory whose originators (Acemoglu, Levy, Murnane) are outside the credited set. The Scientific Background should address the persistence re-analyses directly. P002 (B012: Melitz, Helpman) is a close second. Its core mechanism is mature and confirmed on firm microdata, but credit is exposed to the parallel Bernard-Jensen and Eaton-Kortum work, and I weigh that as roughly comparable to B022's attribution limits. I would not oppose it. P000 is last because both proposals describe substantial, well-tested discoveries that meet the standard for an award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. My co-authors and collaborators in matching, kidney exchange, refugee resettlement, school choice and auctions are not credited on B022 or B012. I note Lund colleague Kerstin Enflo and SSE affiliations with some committee colleagues, none connected to any credited candidate. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
